title: Resilient disconnect recovery and compact cleanup for partial streaming generations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Clients frequently disconnect mid-generation (network blips, mobile backgrounding, browser tab close). Currently we either hold resources for long TTLs or aggressively GC partial outputs and KV cache, both causing either wasted GPU time or poor resume UX and lost partial results. This ticket implements a middle-ground: a lease+grace recovery system with compact cleanup for partial generations that preserves resumability for a bounded window while enabling predictable memory/GPU reclaiming.
design_summary: We introduce a small state machine for each in-flight generation: Active -> Detached (client disconnected but generation may continue) -> Quarantined (no client & low-likelihood resume) -> Tombstoned (final GC). Key components: 1) Short-lived resume leases (resume token with epoch, ttl, checksum) that clients can present to reattach; 2) Ephemeral prefix/KV snapshotting to allow resuming mid-KV-cache with continuity; 3) Adaptive grace period heuristics derived from request size, model latency, and user tier; 4) Compact cleanup job that coalesces partial outputs into a minimal tombstone record for auditing and metric computation and frees GPU memory. This is compatible with function/tool calling and structured outputs: tool call semantic boundaries are atomically checkpointed (can't leave a dangling function call half-applied), and structured outputs are stored as incremental deltas so resumed sessions reconstruct a deterministic final payload.
acceptance_criteria: Resumable sessions: clients presenting a valid resume token within the adaptive grace period can continue generation and get identical final structured output as if never disconnected
Resource reclaim: ephemeral KV cache and generation memory reclaimed within configured SLA (default 60s for P0, 180s for P1 customers) after tombstone transition

No tool-call leakage: function/tool calls invoked before disconnect are either completed, rolled back, or placed into a safe retry queue, with no duplicated external side-effects in typical resume flow
Observability: new metrics (resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, average_grace_duration, tombstone_count) emitted and visible in Console dashboards
Compatibility: feature gated for older SDKs—fallback behavior matches existing semantics when resume token is not supported
release_notes: Adds resumable streaming sessions with adaptive grace periods and compact tombstone cleanup. Feature is behind runtime flag and SDK opt-in; no behavioral changes until enabled.
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after postmortem for INC-2026-02-stream-drop. Proposal includes lease tokens + compact tombstones. Linked design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Resume+Tokens+and+Compact+Cleanup

2026-02-12 Liam O'Connor: Spike completed — validated resume token design in local harness. Found edge case where tool-call side-effects could be duplicated if server restarted between tool call ack and client commit. Proposed solution: durable tool-call phase with at-least-once semantics and idempotency keys enforced at gateway.

2026-02-16 Engineering review: agreed on 3s heartbeat extension for mobile SDKs and per-customer adaptive TTLs. Decided to implement tombstone compaction in two passes: immediate metadata tombstoning + background blob compactor. See RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/412

2026-02-20 Design review (Marina Chen): structured output delta format approved; format v1 will put array of atomic deltas with offsets to allow deterministic reassembly. Design note: function call boundaries must be persisted in checkpoint deltas.

2026-02-23 Implementation update (Liam): core state machine implemented in serving runtime; added resume token generation and verification (HMAC epoch-based). Still TODO: KV snapshot checkpointing and tests for tool-call idempotency.

2026-02-25 QA: integration tests scaffolding added; scenario matrix includes abrupt TCP disconnect, TLS renegotiate, browser pagehide, and SDK background suspend. Found race where resume token TTL not extended on background reconnect; fixed by extending TTL on reconnection handshake.

2026-02-28 Ops: Load test run on staging (1k sustained streams with 8% disconnect rate) shows 18% reduction in long-lived memory compared to baseline TTL=300s, and resume success rate at 94% for same-session reconnects.

2026-03-01 Code review: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891 opened. Requested: clearer metrics tags (customer_tier, model_family) and unit tests around function-call rollback semantics. Assigned to @liam for follow-up.

2026-03-01 Product note (Jorge Alvarez): Feature gating desired per-customer and per-route; we'll expose default grace settings in Console with an advanced toggle. Add to Console rollout epic if runtime-1.21 is selected for GA.
